stem: According to Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, all human beings are born:
choices: subject to the laws of their country
free and equal in dignity and rights
explanation: Article 1 of the UDHR states that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights, endowed with reason and conscience.
quote: All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights.

stem: Article 3 of the UDHR guarantees everyone the right to:
choices: work, fair wages and paid holidays
life, liberty and security of person
explanation: Article 3 of the UDHR states: "Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person." The other choices are real UDHR rights, but they appear in other articles.
quote: Everyone has the right to life, liberty and security of person.

stem: Which UDHR article provides that no one shall be held in slavery or servitude?
explanation: Article 4 states that no one shall be held in slavery or servitude, and that slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.
quote: No one shall be held in slavery or servitude; slavery and the slave trade shall be prohibited in all their forms.

stem: Under Article 5 of the UDHR, no one shall be subjected to:
choices: taxation without representation in a national legislature
compulsory military service in time of peace or war
compulsory education beyond the elementary stages
torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment
explanation: Article 5 of the UDHR prohibits torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.
quote: No one shall be subjected to torture or to cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment or punishment.

stem: Article 9 of the UDHR states that no one shall be subjected to arbitrary:
explanation: Article 9 provides that no one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest, detention or exile.
quote: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary arrest, detention or exile.

stem: Under Article 11 of the UDHR, everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be:
choices: presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial
released on bail in all cases, regardless of the gravity of the offence
pardoned for a first offence if they show sincere repentance in court
tried by a jury chosen by the accused from among their own community
explanation: Article 11 guarantees the presumption of innocence until proved guilty according to law in a public trial with all guarantees necessary for the defence.
quote: Everyone charged with a penal offence has the right to be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law in a public trial

stem: Under Article 14 of the UDHR, everyone has the right to seek and to enjoy in other countries:
explanation: Article 14 recognizes the right to seek and enjoy asylum from persecution, which cannot be invoked for genuinely non-political crimes.
quote: Everyone has the right to seek and to enjoy in other countries asylum from persecution.

stem: Article 15 of the UDHR provides that everyone has the right to:
explanation: Article 15 states that everyone has the right to a nationality and that no one shall be arbitrarily deprived of it.
quote: Everyone has the right to a nationality.

stem: According to Article 16 of the UDHR, marriage shall be entered into only with:
choices: the free and full consent of the intending spouses
explanation: Article 16 requires the free and full consent of the intending spouses and calls the family the natural and fundamental group unit of society.
quote: Marriage shall be entered into only with the free and full consent of the intending spouses.

stem: Under Article 20 of the UDHR, which statement is true about associations?
choices: No one may be compelled to belong to an association
Everyone must join at least one association
explanation: Article 20 guarantees freedom of peaceful assembly and association, and states that no one may be compelled to belong to an association.
quote: No one may be compelled to belong to an association.

stem: Article 21 of the UDHR recognizes everyone's right of equal access to:
explanation: Article 21 states that everyone has the right of equal access to public service in his country, and that the will of the people is the basis of the authority of government.
quote: Everyone has the right of equal access to public service in his country.

stem: Article 23 of the UDHR provides that everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to:
explanation: Article 23 guarantees the right to work, to free choice of employment, and to equal pay for equal work, without discrimination.
quote: Everyone, without any discrimination, has the right to equal pay for equal work.

stem: Article 24 of the UDHR recognizes the right to rest and leisure, including:
choices: reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic holidays with pay
early retirement with full pay after twenty years of service
a four-day work week and an additional month of pay every year
unlimited sick leave and free travel during public holidays
explanation: Article 24 states that everyone has the right to rest and leisure, including reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic holidays with pay.
quote: Everyone has the right to rest and leisure, including reasonable limitation of working hours and periodic holidays with pay.

stem: Under Article 26 of the UDHR, education shall be free at least in the:
explanation: Article 26 provides that education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages, and that elementary education shall be compulsory.
quote: Education shall be free, at least in the elementary and fundamental stages.

stem: According to Article 26 of the UDHR, who has a prior right to choose the kind of education given to their children?
explanation: Article 26 states that parents have a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their children.
quote: Parents have a prior right to choose the kind of education that shall be given to their children.

stem: Article 29 of the UDHR states that, in exercising their rights and freedoms, everyone shall be subject only to limitations that are:
choices: imposed by the executive during a state of emergency to protect public order and national security
set by each nation's courts to balance individual freedoms against the interests of the majority
determined by law to secure respect for the rights of others and to meet the just requirements of the general welfare
agreed upon by the United Nations General Assembly to preserve international peace and security
explanation: Article 29 allows only limitations determined by law solely to secure due recognition and respect for the rights and freedoms of others and to meet the just requirements of morality, public order and the general welfare in a democratic society.
quote: everyone shall be subject only to such limitations as are determined by law solely for the purpose of securing due recognition and respect for the rights and freedoms of others

stem: Article 12 of the UDHR protects against arbitrary interference with a person's:
choices: criminal record, debts or court cases
explanation: Article 12 states that no one shall be subjected to arbitrary interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence, nor to attacks upon his honour and reputation.
quote: No one shall be subjected to arbitrary interference with his privacy, family, home or correspondence

stem: Under Article 13 of the UDHR, everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to:
explanation: Article 13 guarantees freedom of movement within a state and the right to leave any country, including one's own, and to return to one's country.
quote: Everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country.

stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, which body may investigate all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights, on its own or on complaint?
choices: The Department of Social Welfare and Development
explanation: Article XIII, Section 18 empowers the Commission on Human Rights to investigate, on its own or on complaint by any party, all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights.
quote: all forms of human rights violations involving civil and political rights

stem: The 1987 Constitution provides that the State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees:
explanation: Article II, Section 11 states that the State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees full respect for human rights.
quote: The State values the dignity of every human person and guarantees full respect for human rights.

stem: Under Article III, Section 12(2) of the Constitution, which of the following is prohibited against a person under investigation?
choices: Being informed of the right to counsel
Torture, force, violence, threat or intimidation
explanation: Article III, Section 12(2) states that no torture, force, violence, threat, intimidation, or any other means which vitiate the free will shall be used against such person.
quote: No torture, force, violence, threat, intimidation, or any other means which vitiate the free will shall be used against him.

stem: Under Article III, Section 13 of the Constitution, the right to bail shall not be impaired even when:
choices: the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus is suspended
the accused is a public official
explanation: Article III, Section 13 states that the right to bail shall not be impaired even when the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus is suspended.
quote: The right to bail shall not be impaired even when the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus is suspended.

stem: Article III, Section 18 of the Constitution states that no person shall be detained solely by reason of his:
explanation: Article III, Section 18(1) provides that no person shall be detained solely by reason of his political beliefs and aspirations.
quote: No person shall be detained solely by reason of his political beliefs and aspirations.

stem: Under Article III, Section 18(2), involuntary servitude in any form shall not exist EXCEPT as:
choices: a punishment for a crime of which the party has been duly convicted
a requirement of military training during a declared state of war
a means of paying off debts owed to a private employer
a form of community service ordered by the barangay
explanation: Article III, Section 18(2) prohibits involuntary servitude except as punishment for a crime for which the party has been duly convicted.
quote: No involuntary servitude in any form shall exist except as a punishment for a crime whereof the party shall have been duly convicted.

stem: Under Article 2 of the UDHR, everyone is entitled to the rights and freedoms in the Declaration:
choices: without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex or religion
subject to the approval of their national government
only if they are citizens of an independent state
only after reaching the age of majority
explanation: Article 2 entitles everyone to the Declaration's rights "without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion," and adds that no distinction may be made based on the status of a person's country or territory.
quote: Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind

stem: Article 6 of the UDHR states that everyone has the right to recognition everywhere as:
choices: a citizen of the country of his birth
explanation: Article 6 reads: "Everyone has the right to recognition everywhere as a person before the law."
quote: Everyone has the right to recognition everywhere as a person before the law.

stem: According to Article 7 of the UDHR, all are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to:
choices: the same wage for any kind of work
an equal share of national wealth
explanation: Article 7 provides that "All are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law."
quote: All are equal before the law and are entitled without any discrimination to equal protection of the law.

stem: Under Article 8 of the UDHR, a person whose fundamental rights granted by the constitution or by law are violated has the right to:
choices: an effective remedy by the competent national tribunals
compensation paid by the United Nations
asylum in any country of his choice
a pardon from the head of state
explanation: Article 8 gives everyone "the right to an effective remedy by the competent national tribunals" for acts violating fundamental rights granted by the constitution or by law.
quote: Everyone has the right to an effective remedy by the competent national tribunals for acts violating the fundamental rights granted him by the constitution or by law.

stem: Article 10 of the UDHR entitles everyone, in full equality, to a fair and public hearing by:
choices: the head of his local government
explanation: Article 10 provides for "a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal" in determining a person's rights, obligations and any criminal charge.
quote: Everyone is entitled in full equality to a fair and public hearing by an independent and impartial tribunal

stem: Article 17 of the UDHR provides that no one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his:
explanation: Article 17 recognizes the right to own property alone or with others and states: "No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property."
quote: No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of his property.

stem: Under Article 18 of the UDHR, the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion includes the freedom to:
choices: be exempt from taxes on religious grounds
refuse to obey any law that conflicts with his faith
explanation: Article 18 states that the right "includes freedom to change his religion or belief" and to manifest it in teaching, practice, worship and observance.
quote: this right includes freedom to change his religion or belief

stem: Article 19 of the UDHR states that the freedom of opinion and expression includes the freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and:
explanation: Article 19 protects the freedom "to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and regardless of frontiers."
quote: to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and regardless of frontiers

stem: Under Article 22 of the UDHR, everyone, as a member of society, has the right to:
choices: free housing provided by the State
explanation: Article 22 begins: "Everyone, as a member of society, has the right to social security."
quote: Everyone, as a member of society, has the right to social security

stem: Article 25 of the UDHR states that which two are entitled to special care and assistance?
explanation: Article 25(2) reads: "Motherhood and childhood are entitled to special care and assistance." Old age and disability appear in Article 25(1) only as circumstances in which a person has a right to security.
quote: Motherhood and childhood are entitled to special care and assistance.

stem: According to Article 25 of the UDHR, all children, whether born in or out of wedlock, shall enjoy:
choices: citizenship in the country of their birth
the same inheritance from both parents
explanation: Article 25(2) provides: "All children, whether born in or out of wedlock, shall enjoy the same social protection."
quote: All children, whether born in or out of wedlock, shall enjoy the same social protection.

stem: Which right does Article 27 of the UDHR recognize?
choices: To a paid vacation every month
To own land in any country
To participate freely in the cultural life of the community
explanation: Article 27 gives everyone the right "freely to participate in the cultural life of the community, to enjoy the arts and to share in scientific advancement and its benefits."
quote: Everyone has the right freely to participate in the cultural life of the community

stem: Article 30 of the UDHR states that nothing in the Declaration may be interpreted as implying any right to:
choices: engage in any activity aimed at the destruction of the rights and freedoms set forth in it
form or join a political party
explanation: Article 30 bars reading the Declaration as giving any State, group or person a right "to engage in any activity or to perform any act aimed at the destruction of any of the rights and freedoms set forth herein." Criticizing the government, leaving one's country and joining associations are protected rights.
quote: any right to engage in any activity or to perform any act aimed at the destruction of any of the rights and freedoms set forth herein

stem: Which statement is consistent with Article III, Section 5 of the 1987 Constitution?
choices: A religious test may be required before a person can vote.
The State shall adopt an official national religion.
No law shall be made respecting an establishment of religion.
Religious groups need a government license before holding worship services.
explanation: Section 5 provides that "No law shall be made respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof," and that no religious test shall be required for the exercise of civil or political rights.
quote: No law shall be made respecting an establishment of religion, or prohibiting the free exercise thereof.

stem: Under Article III, Section 6 of the Constitution, the right to travel may be impaired only in the interest of:
choices: national security, public safety, or public health
explanation: Section 6 states that the right to travel shall not be impaired "except in the interest of national security, public safety, or public health, as may be provided by law."
quote: Neither shall the right to travel be impaired except in the interest of national security, public safety, or public health, as may be provided by law.

stem: Under Article III, Section 8 of the Constitution, the right to form unions, associations or societies for purposes not contrary to law belongs to the people, including those employed in:
explanation: Section 8 protects the right of the people, "including those employed in the public and private sectors," to form unions, associations, or societies for purposes not contrary to law.
quote: The right of the people, including those employed in the public and private sectors, to form unions, associations, or societies for purposes not contrary to law shall not be abridged.

stem: Article III, Section 11 of the Constitution provides that free access to the courts and adequate legal assistance shall not be denied to any person by reason of:
explanation: Section 11 reads: "Free access to the courts and quasi-judicial bodies and adequate legal assistance shall not be denied to any person by reason of poverty."
quote: Free access to the courts and quasi-judicial bodies and adequate legal assistance shall not be denied to any person by reason of poverty.

stem: Under Article III, Section 14 of the Constitution, after arraignment, trial may proceed even if the accused is absent, provided that:
choices: he has been duly notified and his failure to appear is unjustifiable
the prosecution has already presented all its evidence
the offense is punishable by a fine only
explanation: Section 14(2) allows trial in absentia after arraignment "Provided, that he has been duly notified and his failure to appear is unjustifiable."
quote: after arraignment, trial may proceed notwithstanding the absence of the accused: Provided, that he has been duly notified and his failure to appear is unjustifiable.

stem: Article III, Section 15 of the Constitution allows the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus to be suspended only in cases of:
choices: invasion or rebellion, when the public safety requires it
explanation: Section 15 reads: "The privilege of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended except in cases of invasion or rebellion, when the public safety requires it."
quote: The privilege of the writ of habeas corpus shall not be suspended except in cases of invasion or rebellion, when the public safety requires it.

stem: Under Article III, Section 13 of the Constitution, which persons are NOT entitled to bail before conviction?
choices: All persons arrested during a suspension of the writ of habeas corpus
Those charged with offenses punishable by reclusion perpetua when evidence of guilt is strong
All persons charged with offenses punishable by more than six years of imprisonment
Those charged with offenses punishable by reclusion perpetua, however weak the evidence
explanation: Section 13 makes all persons bailable before conviction "except those charged with offenses punishable by reclusion perpetua when evidence of guilt is strong." It also says the right to bail is not impaired even when the writ of habeas corpus is suspended.
quote: All persons, except those charged with offenses punishable by reclusion perpetua when evidence of guilt is strong, shall, before conviction, be bailable by sufficient sureties

stem: Article III, Section 16 of the Constitution guarantees all persons the right to a speedy disposition of their cases before:
choices: the Office of the Ombudsman only
all judicial, quasi-judicial, or administrative bodies
explanation: Section 16 covers cases "before all judicial, quasi-judicial, or administrative bodies," not only courts.
quote: All persons shall have the right to a speedy disposition of their cases before all judicial, quasi-judicial, or administrative bodies.

stem: "No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself." Article III, Section 17 of the Constitution protects the right against:
explanation: Being compelled to testify against oneself is self-incrimination. Double jeopardy is Section 21, unreasonable searches Section 2, and ex post facto laws Section 22.
quote: No person shall be compelled to be a witness against himself.

stem: Under Article III, Section 12 of the Constitution, which form of detention is expressly prohibited?
choices: Detention of an accused charged with a non-bailable offense
Detention after conviction by final judgment
explanation: Section 12(2) provides: "Secret detention places, solitary, incommunicado, or other similar forms of detention are prohibited."
quote: Secret detention places, solitary, incommunicado, or other similar forms of detention are prohibited.

stem: Under Article III, Section 12 of the Constitution, a person under investigation may waive the right to remain silent and to counsel only:
choices: in writing before a notary public
in writing and in the presence of counsel
in the presence of a family member
explanation: Section 12(1) states that these rights "cannot be waived except in writing and in the presence of counsel."
quote: These rights cannot be waived except in writing and in the presence of counsel.

stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, the Commission on Human Rights is composed of:
explanation: Article XIII, Section 17 provides that the Commission "shall be composed of a Chairman and four Members who must be natural-born citizens of the Philippines."
quote: The Commission shall be composed of a Chairman and four Members who must be natural-born citizens of the Philippines and a majority of whom shall be members of the Bar.

stem: The Commission on Human Rights exercises visitorial powers over:
explanation: Article XIII, Section 18(4) gives the Commission the power to "Exercise visitorial powers over jails, prisons, or detention facilities."
quote: Exercise visitorial powers over jails, prisons, or detention facilities;

stem: Which power does the Commission on Human Rights have under Article XIII, Section 18 of the Constitution?
choices: Prosecute and convict violators of human rights
Grant immunity from prosecution to a person whose testimony is necessary to determine the truth in its investigation
Reverse decisions of the Supreme Court in human rights cases
Issue warrants of arrest against suspected violators
explanation: Section 18(8) lets the Commission grant immunity from prosecution to anyone whose testimony or evidence is necessary or convenient to determine the truth in its investigation. It investigates, but it cannot convict, issue arrest warrants or overturn court rulings.
quote: Grant immunity from prosecution to any person whose testimony or whose possession of documents or other evidence is necessary or convenient to determine the truth in any investigation conducted by it or under its authority;
